366	#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)
367	
368	**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.
369	
370	**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). Only `LoginPasswordlessUser` is affected. `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` is empty — no Zimmermann code merges anything.
371	
372	**Changes.** Add a Zimmermann-owned `mergeBasket` call in `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
373	
374	**Corrected 2026-09-19, before this step's Implementer was dispatched — the exact call site above was wrong, found by reading base's real mechanism instead of this paragraph's own original summary of it.** This originally said "at the point `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds... around line 230" (i.e., inside `handleOtpVerification`). Base's own `use-auth-modal.js` does **not** call `handleMergeBasket` from its own equivalent of `handleOtpVerification` at all — it calls it from a separate `useEffect(() => {...}, [isRegistered])` that fires once the customer's registered state actually flips true, paired with `onLoginSuccess()`. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` already has the exact structural equivalent of that effect (its own `isRegistered` effect that calls `onClose()`/`onAuthSuccess?.()`) — the merge call belongs there, alongside `onAuthSuccess?.()`, not inside `handleOtpVerification`. Reasoning: `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` resolving only means the SDK set the session; `isRegistered` (derived from `useCustomerType()`) is the signal that the rest of the customer-dependent state has actually caught up, which is presumably why base itself waits for it rather than firing merge directly off the raw mutation promise.
375	
376	Also corrected the same day: base additionally gates its own call on `hasBasketItem && prevAuthType === 'guest'` (via `useCustomerBaskets` + `usePrevious(customerType)`) — skip a pointless merge call when the guest basket is empty. This build deliberately does **not** replicate that guard (Marcel's call, 2026-09-19, asked directly): the `prevAuthType === 'guest'` half is already structurally guaranteed here for free — `handleTriggerClick` never opens this drawer at all when the customer is already registered, so every path that can reach the `isRegistered` effect's merge call started from a guest session by construction, with no `usePrevious` needed. The `hasBasketItem` half is deliberately skipped: replicating it would mean wiring a brand-new basket-loading dependency into a hook that has never needed one, on a step already flagged (pass criterion 4 below) as having no CODEOWNERS coverage to catch a subtle timing mistake — and the failure mode of getting that new dependency's timing wrong (merge silently skipped when it shouldn't be) is the exact "shopper's items are gone" bug this whole step exists to close. The failure mode of *not* having the check (one occasional harmless merge-call on an empty basket) is strictly cheaper. Call unconditionally inside the effect; no `useCustomerBaskets`, no `usePrevious`, no `customerType` needed.
377	
378	`sum_quantities`, not the SDK default `higher_quantity`, because AC5's "combined quantity exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. **This changes every merge, not just over-max ones** — a guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it: today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. It must go in a comment on SFCC-250 (deferred to post-build) because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to know two items is intended.
379	
380	**Pass criteria.**
381	1. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` asserts `mergeBasket` is called exactly once on passwordless success, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
382	2. It asserts `mergeBasket` is **not** called on the create-account route (base deliberately skips register).
383	3. It asserts the social-IDP route is untouched — no second merge added on top of base `social-login-redirect`'s.
384	4. **Regression gate on the other three consumers.** The hook is consumed by `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view` and (new) the cart. Existing tests for all four still pass, and the PR body names all four as the change's blast radius. This is a shared hook with four call sites and **no CODEOWNERS entry** (see open question 3) — the review that would normally catch a mistake here is not automatically requested.
385	5. The hook's exported signature is **unchanged**. A signature change would need a team RFC (AGENTS.md "When to Stop").
386	6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.
387	
388	#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`
389	
390	**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.
391	
392	Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.
393	
394	**Pass criteria.**
395	1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
396	2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
397	3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
398	4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
399	5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
400	6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.
401	
402	#### Step 4.3 — `useCartMessages`: one handler, one file to swap
403	
404	**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.
405	
406	Interim surface is the base Chakra toast. **See open question 4 before writing the import line** — `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist, and creating it is a Tier 2 change this bundle has not budgeted for.
407	
408	Copy (Figma leading, per the cards): single message uses the **product-named** variant, "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist"; already-in-wishlist is "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist"; max-reached is "An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity". The generic stacked variant ("Item added to Wishlist") is only reachable once 404 lands with real stacking — a toast has no aggregation concept and is always on its own from the shopper's point of view, so the **interim toast uses the product-named copy**. Both divergences from SFCC-272's AC wording go on the deferred Jira comment; the cards are not edited.
409	
410	**Pass criteria.**
411	1. `grep -rn "useToast\|toast(" overrides/app/pages/cart overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart* overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts` shows exactly **one** emit site. **Path corrected 2026-09-20**, before this step's Implementer was dispatched: the original two paths never included `overrides/app/hooks/`, but B4's own manifest puts this step's file at `overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts` — the literal grep as first written would find zero matches even once built correctly, not the "exactly one" it was checking for. Confirmed via a real grep of all three paths today: zero existing `useToast`/`toast(` usage anywhere in them, so adding the hook's own file to the scope can't accidentally inflate the count past one.
412	2. Each of the three copy strings is asserted verbatim in a test.
413	3. A Storybook `play` asserting a message queries `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing `testing.md`'s portal exception — Chakra toasts portal outside `canvasElement` and this is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`. **Deferred, not met by this step — flagged 2026-09-20 by this step's own Tester as a real gap in the plan text, not just in the build.** `useCartMessages.ts` is a hook, and this codebase has zero `.stories.tsx` files anywhere under `overrides/app/hooks/` — a `play` function needs a rendered, clickable component to assert against, and nothing renders a message-triggering UI yet (that's steps 4.4/4.6, neither built). This criterion is almost certainly a drafting leftover from before B4's manifest was scoped down to "hook only, wiring deferred" — the immediately preceding hook-only step (4.2, `useCartMergeAndCap`) has zero Storybook-related criteria at all, consistent with `components.md`'s own rule that only components/pages need stories. Move this proof to whichever of step 4.4/4.6 first renders a component that actually triggers one of these three messages — do not build a throwaway demo component here just to satisfy it early.
414	4. The SFCC-404 marker comment is present and names the ticket.

This build deliberately does **not** replicate that guard (Marcel's call, 2026-09-19, asked directly): the `prevAuthType === 'guest'` half is already structurally guaranteed here for free — `handleTriggerClick` never opens this drawer at all when the customer is already registered, so every path that can reach the `isRegistered` effect's merge call started from a guest session by construction, with no `usePrevious` needed. The `hasBasketItem` half is deliberately skipped: replicating it would mean wiring a brand-new basket-loading dependency into a hook that has never needed one, on a step already flagged (pass criterion 4 below) as having no CODEOWNERS coverage to catch a subtle timing mistake — and the failure mode of getting that new dependency's timing wrong (merge silently skipped when it shouldn't be) is the exact "shopper's items are gone" bug this whole step exists to close. The failure mode of *not* having the check (one occasional harmless merge-call on an empty basket) is strictly cheaper. Call unconditionally inside the effect; no `useCustomerBaskets`, no `usePrevious`, no `customerType` needed.

`sum_quantities`, not the SDK default `higher_quantity`, because AC5's "combined quantity exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. **This changes every merge, not just over-max ones** — a guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it: today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. It must go in a comment on SFCC-250 (deferred to post-build) because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to know two items is intended.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` asserts `mergeBasket` is called exactly once on passwordless success, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
2. It asserts `mergeBasket` is **not** called on the create-account route (base deliberately skips register).
3. It asserts the social-IDP route is untouched — no second merge added on top of base `social-login-redirect`'s.
4. **Regression gate on the other three consumers.** The hook is consumed by `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view` and (new) the cart. Existing tests for all four still pass, and the PR body names all four as the change's blast radius. This is a shared hook with four call sites and **no CODEOWNERS entry** (see open question 3) — the review that would normally catch a mistake here is not automatically requested.
5. The hook's exported signature is **unchanged**. A signature change would need a team RFC (AGENTS.md "When to Stop").
6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.

#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`

**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.

Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.

#### Step 4.3 — `useCartMessages`: one handler, one file to swap

**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.

Interim surface is the base Chakra toast. **See open question 4 before writing the import line** — `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist, and creating it is a Tier 2 change this bundle has not budgeted for.

Copy (Figma leading, per the cards): single message uses the **product-named** variant, "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist"; already-in-wishlist is "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist"; max-reached is "An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity". The generic stacked variant ("Item added to Wishlist") is only reachable once 404 lands with real stacking — a toast has no aggregation concept and is always on its own from the shopper's point of view, so the **interim toast uses the product-named copy**. Both divergences from SFCC-272's AC wording go on the deferred Jira comment; the cards are not edited.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `grep -rn "useToast\|toast(" overrides/app/pages/cart overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart* overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts` shows exactly **one** emit site. **Path corrected 2026-09-20**, before this step's Implementer was dispatched: the original two paths never included `overrides/app/hooks/`, but B4's own manifest puts this step's file at `overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts` — the literal grep as first written would find zero matches even once built correctly, not the "exactly one" it was checking for. Confirmed via a real grep of all three paths today: zero existing `useToast`/`toast(` usage anywhere in them, so adding the hook's own file to the scope can't accidentally inflate the count past one.
2. Each of the three copy strings is asserted verbatim in a test.
3. A Storybook `play` asserting a message queries `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing `testing.md`'s portal exception — Chakra toasts portal outside `canvasElement` and this is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`. **Deferred, not met by this step — flagged 2026-09-20 by this step's own Tester as a real gap in the plan text, not just in the build.** `useCartMessages.ts` is a hook, and this codebase has zero `.stories.tsx` files anywhere under `overrides/app/hooks/` — a `play` function needs a rendered, clickable component to assert against, and nothing renders a message-triggering UI yet (that's steps 4.4/4.6, neither built). import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the "Remove" / "Move to Wishlist" action-links row (SFCC-270 AC8, SFCC-272). Single
 * style, no parts: both links get their full visual treatment from `ZimmLink`'s own recipe
 * (`zimmLink.css.ts`, size `small` — capitalize, 12px/500/14px-lh, plus that recipe's own
 * hover/focus-visible states); this recipe only owns the row's own layout, matching
 * `zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts`'s own single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` — Figma specifies 25px (§11.10(4) of the SFCC-11 plan); no `--zimm-scale-*` step lands on
 * 25 (foundation/spacing.ts's steps go ...m:16px, l:20px, xl:24px, 2xl:32px... — confirmed no
 * 25px entry), so this snaps to the nearest existing token, 24px (`xl`), and records the raw
 * design value here rather than typing an unregistered one-off literal.
 *
 * `color` on each link is NOT set here: `ZimmLink`'s own `link.default` alias
 * (`foundation/colour.ts:87`, `grey[900]`) and `foundation/colour.ts:61`'s `text.default` (also
 * `grey[900]`) are the same primitive, so plain `<ZimmLink>` already renders the colour this
 * component's own spec calls for — adding a second, competing colour declaration here would be
 * exactly the anti-pattern `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "One canonical styling surface
 * per component type" section warns against (a value that can drift from the atom's own recipe
 * over time instead of there being only one place it's declared).
 */
export const ZimmCartItemActions = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // Figma: 25px, snapped to the nearest token (24px)
  },
});

2	import {
3	  clearSessionJSONItem,

5	  setSessionJSONItem,
6	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils';
7	
8	/**
9	 * Outcome of one wishlist-move attempt. The actual SFCC SDK calls (wishlist add + cart removal)
10	 * are the caller's own responsibility — SFCC-11 plan step 4.6 (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, not
11	 * built yet) — this file only reports what happened, matching the exact discriminated-union
12	 * pattern `useCartMergeAndCap.ts`'s own `CartCapResult` already established
13	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useCartMergeAndCap.ts:25-29`), per typescript.md's stated preference for
14	 * a discriminated union over a pile of optional fields.
15	 */
16	export type WishlistMoveResult =
17	  | { status: 'success' }
18	  | { status: 'already-in-wishlist' }
19	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
20	
21	/**
22	 * sessionStorage key PREFIX for "a guest asked to move THIS specific cart line to their wishlist
23	 * before authenticating." Namespaced per `productId` — see `pendingWishlistCartItemKey` below —
24	 * so that two different cart rows' pending intents can never collide in a single shared slot: a
25	 * guest beginning a pending move on row A, then row B, before either completes a redirect-based
26	 * auth flow, must leave both independently resumable rather than row B's write silently
27	 * overwriting row A's. Deliberately a distinct mechanism, and a distinct key, from
28	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY`
29	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:43`): that key answers "which mounted drawer
30	 * instance's `onAuthSuccess` should fire after a social-IDP redirect" — its own
31	 * `PendingWishlistIntent` type carries only `intentId`/`timestamp`, no item identity at all.
32	 * This hook answers a different question — "which cart LINE was pending" — so it is a new,
33	 * separate mechanism rather than an addition to that shared type. The SFCC-11 plan explicitly
34	 * rejects adding an `itemId` field to that shared type: it has three other existing call sites
35	 * (header/rightBar, drawer-menu, product-view) and changing it is out of this step's scope.
36	 */
37	const PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX = 'zimmPendingWishlistCartItem';
38	
39	/**
40	 * Builds the per-product sessionStorage key — see `PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX`'s own
41	 * doc for why storage is namespaced this way instead of one shared key.
42	 */
43	const pendingWishlistCartItemKey = (productId: string): string =>
44	  `${PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX}:${productId}`;
45	
46	/**
47	 * Same 5-minute bound as `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`
48	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:52` — `5 * 60 * 1000`), and the same reasoning:
49	 * long enough for a real auth round trip, short enough that a long-abandoned attempt cannot
50	 * misfire later against a much later, unrelated cart session. Not imported from that file — the
51	 * constant is not exported there, and this step does not modify that file (out of scope; see the
52	 * SFCC-11 plan step 4.4's manifest and its "explicitly rejected" list). Redefined here as an
53	 * independent, same-valued constant instead.
54	 */
55	const PENDING_WISHLIST_MAX_AGE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes
56	
57	type PendingWishlistCartItem = {
58	  /**
59	   * Matched against this row's own `productId`, not `itemId` — deliberate. A guest's basket may
60	   * be merged into a registered customer's basket between the guest's click and the shopper
61	   * completing auth (SFCC-250 step 4.1, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `isRegistered` effect),
62	   * and that merge can change which `itemId` a given product line carries (it merges into a
63	   * destination basket via `createDestinationBasket: true`). `productId` is stable across that
64	   * boundary; `itemId` is not — keying the match on `itemId` would risk silently failing to
65	   * resume a legitimate pending move the moment a merge has actually happened. See this step's
66	   * own report for the related, still-open sequencing question this raises for step 4.6.
67	   */
68	  productId: string;
69	  timestamp: number;
70	};
71	
72	export type UsePendingWishlistItemParams = {
73	  /** Identifies this cart line for matching a resumed intent — see PendingWishlistCartItem's own
74	   *  doc comment for why this is `productId`, not `itemId`. */
75	  productId: string;
76	  /** Whether the current shopper is unauthenticated. Passed down from the caller (e.g. read once
77	   *  from `useCustomerType()` at the cart container) rather than read by this hook itself — see
78	   *  `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx`'s own architecture note for why. */
79	  isGuest: boolean;
80	  /** Called (no arguments) once a previously-pending move for THIS row should be attempted.
81	   *  Fires at most once per stored intent — never for another row's pending item, never twice
82	   *  for the same one. */
83	  onResume: () => void | Promise<void>;
84	};
85	
86	export type UsePendingWishlistItemReturn = {
87	  /** Call when a guest clicks "Move to Wishlist" for this row — persists the pending intent to
88	   *  both React state (survives the email-code/create-account flows, which never unload the
89	   *  page) and session storage (survives the Apple/Google redirect, which reloads it), so
90	   *  `onResume` fires automatically once `isGuest` becomes false for this same product. */
91	  beginPendingMove: () => void;
92	};
93	
94	/**
95	 * Hook — persists a guest's "move to wishlist" intent for one cart line across an authentication
96	 * step, and resumes it once the shopper is no longer a guest. Extracted per
97	 * `.claude/rules/components.md`'s extract-to-hook threshold: this is React state plus a
98	 * non-trivial effect (session-storage read/write/clear, a 5-minute age check, resuming after a
99	 * simulated page reload) that would otherwise sit inline in `ZimmCartItemActions`.
100	 *
101	 * Deliberately calls no auth or `commerce-sdk-react` hook itself — `isGuest` arrives as a plain
102	 * prop, and the actual move (`onResume`) is the caller's own already-composed function. Only ONE
103	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer` instance may exist for the whole cart (SFCC-11 plan step 4.4's own
104	 * explicit rejection of "one per line item"), so that real hook cannot live inside a component
105	 * that mounts once per cart line — this hook stays calling-hook-free so it can safely mount once
106	 * per row, alongside it, without reproducing that rejected shape.
107	 *
108	 * @returns `beginPendingMove`, the one function a guest click calls.
109	 */
110	export const usePendingWishlistItem = ({
111	  productId,
112	  isGuest,
113	  onResume,
114	}: UsePendingWishlistItemParams): UsePendingWishlistItemReturn => {
115	  const [pending, setPending] = useState<PendingWishlistCartItem | undefined>(undefined);
116	
117	  const beginPendingMove = () => {
118	    const intent: PendingWishlistCartItem = { productId, timestamp: Date.now() };
119	    setPending(intent);
120	    setSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId), intent);
121	  };
122	
123	  // Mirrors useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts's own redirect-consuming effect (that file's second
124	  // useEffect, [isRegistered]-only deps, overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:252-259) —
125	  // runs on mount and on every `isGuest` change, not only on a true-to-false transition, because
126	  // a fresh mount after a real page reload (Apple/Google redirect) already has `isGuest === false`
127	  // on its very first render, with no transition to observe.
128	  useEffect(() => {
129	    if (isGuest) return;
130	
131	    const stored = getSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId)) as PendingWishlistCartItem | undefined;
132	    // The per-product key above already means `stored` can only ever be what THIS row itself
133	    // wrote — a different row's pending intent lives under its own, different key and is never
134	    // read, resumed, or cleared from here. This productId match is a defensive belt-and-suspenders
135	    // check on top of that (never act on foreign/malformed data even if it somehow ended up in
136	    // this slot), not the mechanism that keeps two rows apart.
137	    const mineFromStorage = stored?.productId === productId ? stored : undefined;
138	    const candidate = pending ?? mineFromStorage;
139	    if (!candidate) return;
140	
141	    // Found something of mine — clear both stores now, regardless of whether it turns out to be
142	    // fresh or stale below (a stale intent must not linger either — nothing resumes it later).
143	    // Only ever clears THIS row's own key — another row's still-pending intent, under its own
144	    // key, is untouched.
145	    setPending(undefined);
146	    clearSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId));
147	
148	    const isFresh = Date.now() - candidate.timestamp <= PENDING_WISHLIST_MAX_AGE_MS;
149	    if (isFresh) {
150	      void onResume();
151	    }
152	  }, [isGuest]);
153	
154	  return { beginPendingMove };
155	};

## Commit order

The step boundaries in §4 **are** the commit boundaries. That is what keeps a ~60-file PR
reviewable: twenty scoped commits are navigable, three are not. Order matters more than it did
under §2 because there is no merge between stages.

| # | Commit | From §4 step |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `chore(ci): SFCC-11 add cart e2e area to qa.yml` | 0 |
| 2 | `feat(icons): SFCC-271 port PlusIcon to zimm.tsx` | §10 (1) |
| 3 | `fix(drawer): SFCC-315 correct ZimmDrawer xLarge width` | 1.1 |
| 4 | `chore(cart): SFCC-270 copy-first product-item + item-variant` | 2.1 — **STOP** |
| 5 | `feat(cart): SFCC-270 restyle override, fix item-name spread order` | 2.2 |
| 6 | `feat(cart): SFCC-315 ZimmCartDrawer organism` | 1.2 |
| 7 | `feat(cart): SFCC-271 ZimmQuantityStepper` | 3.1 |
| 8 | `feat(cart): SFCC-795 ZimmInlineMessage, error and warning states` | 3.2 |
| 9 | `feat(cart): SFCC-795 promotional price and discount label` | 3.3 |
| 10 | `feat(cart): SFCC-250 cartItemMapper and maxOrderQuantity util` | 3.4 |
| 11 | `feat(cart): SFCC-271-250 wire ZimmQuantityStepper and maxOrderQuantity into product-item` | 3.5 (inserted 2026-09-18) |
| 12 | `fix(a11y): SFCC-795 accessibility sweep` | 3.6 (renumbered from 3.5) |
| 13 | `feat(auth): SFCC-250 passwordless basket merge` | 4.1 |
| 14 | `feat(cart): SFCC-250 useCartMergeAndCap` | 4.2 |
| 15 | `feat(cart): SFCC-272 useCartMessages` | 4.3 |
| 16 | `feat(cart): SFCC-272 ZimmCartItemActions and pending-item resume` | 4.4 |
| 17 | `feat(cart): SFCC-272 ZimmCartEmptyState` | 4.5 |
| 18 | `feat(cart): SFCC-275 ZimmCartButtonGroup and Pay marks` | 5.1 |
